This game is such a disjointed lopsided experience. After playing for a while, gameplay gets EXTREMELY repetitive and I find myself really only playing to get to the Nightlord bosses, which are easily the most fun you'll have in this game. Other parts become almost chore-like after you've experienced all this game has to offer, and it currently doesn't have much. And yet, I keep playing it. Rarely do I ever NOT have fun in this game, and when I don't, it's because I'm solo queue with idiots who refuse to acknowledge pings, die, and leave.

When I look at this game objectively, it shouldn't work. Objectively, this game is 95% asset flip that only has a fraction of content I'd expect from a studio like FromSoft. Gameplay mechanics work against each other, game information is obfuscated or otherwise just straight up not communicated to the player at all, and interacting with menus and trying to communicate to teammates is hilariously cumbersome.

Subjectively, though, this game is a blast. The presentation is amazing as always and there are so many opportunities to tweak and screw around with builds and game mechanics that you can't do in any other FromSoft game (well, in a soulslike at least - AC6 has similar build/mechanic depth) and it's for those reasons I keep playing it religiously. This just goes to show you how integral presentation and fundamental gameplay systems are to a gaming experience. There is a lot to be studied here about how, on paper, this game looks like it should be TERRIBLE, and yet, I find myself thinking "this is peak" constantly.

Overall, I think this game is a good play for any non-stick-in-the-mud souls fan.

I applaud FromSoft for stepping outside of their comfort zone and experimenting with new genres, although it does make me sad because this and base game ER feel like the last soulslike hurrah from them.

Nightreign is the perfect game for people that are looking for an ‘Elden Ring endgame’ experience. For when you’ve seen enough of Elden Ring and want a bit more of a faster pace with some randomness and rogue-like elements thrown in, grind out spectacular bosses, assemble builds on different nightfarers or play with friends. Nightreign is a perfect project for a developer like fromsoft, who have put together an arsenal of incredible assets over many years, and to throw them all together in a single game is truly an amazing idea, giving players many different challenges to master and adapt to on the fly. 

The maps have many places to explore. When you start out you will have no idea what’s going on or where to go, but after a few games you will explore places or enemies with items that you didn’t know about before. Together with the relic system, which you will earn after every run, you can put together a build for your preferred playstyle and class, adding some nice background progression. Even though some of these relics can empower you noticeably and flesh out your playstyle, after all it really comes down to mastery of the map and its combat encounters. Players with more experience will always triumph over players with the best relic setup. So experience, skill and awareness are the most important factors after all.

The final bosses of each run, the nightlords, are all incredible and spectacular fights, with most of them giving rewards which can help you on your next run. They all have some kind of elemental or status weakness which the game tells you before a run starts, so you’re able to prepare a relic setup before going in. Everyone will have a different experience with each of these nightlords, so when you’ve bested them once, you can choose to master them in any order you want. And for people looking to see more of these bosses, there is a weekly rotating set of ‘Everdark Sovereigns’, which are empowered versions of the base game bosses with an extra third phase, adding another layer of spectacle and challenge to overcome.
A big thing that I’ve heard people talk about is the lack of seeds in the game, which I agree with. It’s not uncommon to find yourself on the same map as the run before if you’re doing the same nightlord, which means you will see the same locations, field bosses, etc.. I also think it’s strange that each nightlord has certain ‘boss pools’, which means that the bosses you face on night 1 and 2 are always drawn from a small pool, and that pool is dependent on the nightlord you will face. I get that a lot of these pools are for flavour, like the nightlord itself has some kind of control over who to summon to face the nightfarers but I would have preferred for there to be no boss pools and have any night 1 and 2 boss to be able to appear in any seed, just to add some more randomness and making it so running the same nightlord does not get as repetitive.

The ultimate challenge in Nightreign is the Deep of Night mode, where the game cranks up the difficulty and you can earn points to climb up the ranks, going from 1-5, with increasing challenge. For me, this is where the cracks of the game are starting to show. The balance of the encounters are thrown out for the sake of creating difficulty, the mods and bosses will have insane amounts of damage and some red encounters will have crazy bloated health pools. You will have a choice to use special relics and weapon drops which are only usable in DoN which add some good new effects but they will also inflict debuffs on you.
For me personally, DoN was not really the kind endgame I was looking for. I understand that some people love this kind of extremely punishing gameplay in a souls game, but for me it's a bit much. I don’t really care about extreme difficulty, I just enjoy the roguelike experience, mastering the bosses and getting through the game with the tools I get given. Having unbalanced enemies which will just oneshot you for trying things, punishing a certain playstyle or having to add debuffs to my nightfarer to play a mode that is already designed to be more difficult is not my definition of fun. Not to mention some of the unfair mechanics introduced in the DLC which really turn me away from Deep of Night.

As for the DLC, the new nightfarers are great, with especially the Scholar adding a lot more depth to the game, and the Undertaker is one of my new favorites. The Dreglord is definitely high up there as one of my favorite Fromsoft bosses. The new hollows shifting earth is pretty-looking and can be very rewarding if you know what you’re doing. However, as this replaces the entire map, a lot of new players will be very confused as to what to do. So I’m afraid when this shifting earth goes away for players they will likely not return to it, as it’s too unfamiliar.
As for the rest, I’m not too impressed with what the DLC added, I was hoping for SotE weapons to be added so it was a bit disappointing to see no new weapons to try out. As well as the messes that are the Balancers and the new raid events, although rewarding, just sucks to keep having to go through.

One of my biggest gripes with this game is the servers and connection. As the game does not have dedicated servers, it runs on p2p connection. Which in my opinion is kinda unacceptable for a multiplayer focused game in the current year. Some games will be borderline unplayable, with enemies lagging, freezing, stuttering, teleporting, cancelling moves into each other, players disconnecting or being kicked offline, which are among some common issues. If Fromsoft wants Duskbloods to be as successful as Elden ring they’d really need to work together with Nintendo to step it up when it comes to the multiplayer connection and netcode, because in its current state it's not acceptable.

By now I've played the game for about 600 hrs in 2025, and as I can’t get myself to grind any more Deep of Night, I feel like I’ve seen it all.
Before Nightreign released I was sceptical if the formula of Souls + Roguelike would work but after all its become one of my favorite games of all time. I love this game. I love Wylder. I love Undertaker. It has some of my favorite video game bosses and soundtracks ever. I’ve had some of my greatest gaming experiences happen and I’ve played with some of my favorite streamers. For now I’ll be waiting to see if there will be any more new content in 2026.

The game needed a longer playtesting period with a focus on gameplay experience, flexibility and its mechanics. I write this as positive because I believe the developers will make sure to refine the game to meet the players expectations have of this IP. While I share the frustration with many about games being released prematurely, I cannot hide my enjoyment playing this game. 

As for things I find objectively problematic at least for a PC player:
*Optimization, the game even on a high end PC can sometimes underperform.
*Relics tend to have polarizing effects that make a large relic for example be so disharmonized it might aswell be viewed as a medium-tier relic.
*Bosses (not all) have bloated stats not making them hard per say but rather tedious and more like a battle of attrition than an actually difficult boss. This isn't like Fromsoft's usual approach when designing or even balancing enemies, hence why I make the point. 

I'm sure there are other problems and certainly many bugs not mentioned here so I left the comments open for everyone to add to the list and hopefully the developers can see this and adhere to our wishes. Thank you for reading.

It's not better than Elden Ring. It's not worse than Elden Ring. It retains a lot of the same feel, but with more nimble player characters, individualized character skills, and a whole new play concept with much faster pacing. The core experience is multiplayer of course, with rapid, well coordinated fighting, exploring, and looting required to complete full expeditions. Solo play is very hard, but enjoyable. Even when you lose, each attempt is different. interesting and a chance to hone your strategy and reflexes. 

The only negative thing I can say about it, is that it's down right frantic. Elden Ring is slow, relaxing exploration interrupted by short, edge of your seat boss encounters. The pacing on this is blistering. You feel like you're falling behind if you stop a second to read an item description. Coming from an Elden Ring background you're eventually bound to ask yourself "Why am I running for my life in a place that looks line Limgrave?" But, if you aren't always in the mood for a game this fast, you have the original game for that. They're very different games, for very different moods. They likely won't appeal to all the same people either, but mostly, if you like Elden Ring, and give this a chance, I believe you will come to love it. 

Side note: In Elden Ring, the return trip on a boss was generally less than a minute. Sometimes near instant. You could fight someone 40 times in a row if need be, back to back, with the exact same gear available and already leveled. In this game, if you want to fight someone 10 times, you'll have to clear a full 10 day expedition for that practice, and that gap between the encounters can making learning tricky dodges very hard, and it discourages trying creative strategies on Night Lords. 

Overall it's a well tuned game, that plays unlike anything else. I'm not very good, but think I will be coming back to this for a very long time.

Never really liked black and white review systems, Nightreign is an incredibly strange game. You essentially turn the souls series into a roguelike with random loot, add a battle royal style wall the closes you into a small area of the map you are on and you have this game.

There are people that will like this game, and there are those that will justifiably despise it. Having to install a co op mod day one of my purchase to play duos is not ideal, but the game is built with an mmo style team synergy in mind. Healer, tank, ranged dps, dps etc. 

On one hand this game uses reused assets, on the other its a cheaper side project for fromsoft, then on another mutated third hand they have already greenlit dlc BEFORE the game was announced with a set date. A lot of practices from this company as of late are red flags, this game in my opinion is one of them.

The game has crashed multiple times, and easy anti cheat notoriously blue screens computers (including mine). Its performance is honestly not bad aside from the crashes, as my hardware is fairly old (980 ti) and I get solid frames here at 1080p. But this type of performance is inexcusable and honestly easy anti cheat should be able to be turned off if playing with friends as it's incredibly intrusive.
